fcfs.effective_settings: Arrival then integer ID order; seed/population/generations/time limit ignored; objective has no placement tie-break effect.

sjf.effective_settings: Runtime then integer ID order; seed/population/generations/time limit ignored; objective has no placement tie-break effect.

prio.effective_settings: Descending priority tier, then arrival and ID; seed/population/generations/time limit ignored.

exact.effective_settings: Exhaustive GPU assignment search with fixed per-GPU priority/arrival order; time limit 1 second; planning horizon 120 minutes; objective balanced score weights cost=1, energy=0.02, makespan=10, waiting=1, priority=1.

energy.effective_settings: GPU-aware placement with consolidation enabled; consumes planning horizon 120 minutes; seed/population/generations/time limit ignored; consolidation candidate score favors already-used/ACTIVE GPUs.

gpu_aware.effective_settings: GPU-aware placement; consumes planning horizon 120 minutes; seed/population/generations/time limit ignored; balanced greedy score.

genetic.selection: Tournament selection, up to 3 candidates per parent; top 2 elites copied.
genetic.crossover: Applied to every child: prefix-and-fill permutation crossover; GPU assignment preference inherited independently per job with 0.5 probability from either parent.
genetic.fitness: Balanced default GA weights: energy=1, cost=1, makespan=0.5, waiting=0.5, priority=1; unscheduled jobs have a large penalty.

nsga2.selection: Binary tournament by rank/crowding; environmental selection from parent+offspring; scheduled-job count has lexicographic priority.
nsga2.crossover: Applied to every child: prefix-and-fill permutation crossover; GPU assignment preference inherited independently per job with 0.5 probability from either parent.
nsga2.display_solution: With objective=balanced, final selector falls back to cost; the selected candidate remains among maximum scheduled-job-count candidates.

note: The same options object is passed to all eight algorithms. The settings each method actually consumes are documented above; omitted/irrelevant settings are not implied to affect a method.
